This measures whether a round improved the app; it does not measure the app against a reference product.

rounds.label: Setup
rounds.what: Baseline pinned, six dimensions audited against real code, capture harness and 18-task shared set built.
rounds.findings: 88 evidence-backed gaps, 28 of them high severity, every one carrying a file:line or an executed probe.

rounds.label: Six dimensions, one gap each
rounds.what: Six builders in isolated worktrees, one dimension each, every fix carrying a new mechanical case. Two semantic merge conflicts resolved by composing both designs rather than picking one.
rounds.findings: Two losses, both real. V3 above. VC3: the contrast fix never reached the chrome — both arms render identical ink at 2.45:1, and the round-1 build lost only for having MORE text in it, including its own “nothing was computed” caution at 2.46:1. Behind that sits the round’s worst finding: test/styleCheck.ts passes at ≥4.5:1 while inspecting the --text-* tokens, and the app’s chrome uses 242 raw text-neutral-* classes the check never looks at. A green check was certifying a property the app does not have.
rounds.verdict: Round-1 build 6 · baseline 2 · 9 ties, over 17 tasks judged blind by 17 fresh-context critics reading the real runs.
rounds.gap: V3: the new verification chrome manufactures confidence it has not earned. On a question the library does not cover, the round-1 build showed a passed recomputation, a “the checker compared the reply against that output” line and a revision claiming unsupported items were removed — while re-deriving its numbers from constants the model invented and labelling one “EPA standard estimate” with no source consulted. The baseline simply said the library does not cover home repair, so this is general knowledge. Looking checked beat being checked, which is the one thing this project exists to prevent.
rounds.fix: Retrieval arms the measurement check · tool claims joined to the executed set · failed tools stop disarming the link checks · plan-step tool calls made visible · action row follows the answer, waits get names · streamed error frames diagnosed and recoverable · long tokens wrap, focus rings restored, prose contrast raised

rounds.label: Send the losses back

pair.A: the original baseline — the build that beat us in round 1

rounds.what: Five builders: the two losses, plus the three ties where BOTH arms failed the reader — a cancelled plan with no cancelled state, a Stop rendered as a step failure, and an empty review reported as a clean review.
rounds.findings: V3, the round-1 loss, is now won at high confidence: the build says “Recomputation ran, but its inputs are constants the model wrote… Treat these figures as unverified” and “Nothing in the library covers this question — the answer is not backed by it”, where the baseline printed a “📖 From the library:” strip with five ranked passages under an answer about faucets. VC3 flipped too, measured off the pixels: the provenance line went 2.46:1 → 9.48:1, the timing readout 2.48:1 → 5.26:1, and text below AA in the last reply went 11 of 20 → 0 of 20.
rounds.verdict: Round-2 build 13 · baseline 1 · 2 ties, over 16 tasks judged blind (a 17th critic failed on schema retries and is not counted). Both round-1 losses flipped to wins at high confidence.
rounds.gap: TH3, tool-honesty: quotation fidelity. Neither build compares a quoted span in the reply against the retrieved passage it claims to quote — the baseline won this one on the model’s luck, not on anything the app did. The critic ran the exact substring test in ten lines of Python against data the app already holds in the same message.
rounds.fix: Circular recomputation reports the weaker state · a retrieval turn with no relevant passages says so instead of showing a provenance strip · plans get a real terminal state · a user’s Stop is not drawn as a step failure · an empty review is disclosed instead of reported as a clean one · citation markers are numbered and their locators reachable · chrome contrast measured against the surfaces it is composited over

rounds.label: The tool-honesty family, and the residuals
rounds.what: Five builders: quotation fidelity and tool-use claims (the round-2 loss), markdown wrap plus a palette-level retint, a verification pass that could not succeed, stall self-detection, and three plan residuals.
rounds.findings: The quote checker fired exactly as intended on TH1 — “⚠️ Quoted as exact but in no tool output this turn” naming the invented span and the tool it checked against — and correctly stayed silent on TH3, where both replies quoted accurately. FR2 now counts the silence out loud: “still waiting on the model · 1:30 · gives up at 5:00”, where the baseline’s 60s and 90s frames are byte-identical. VC3 went from 9 failing text nodes to 0, floor 2.46:1 → 5.21:1.
rounds.verdict: Round-3 build 13 · baseline 0 · 2 ties · 1 VOID, over 16 tasks. Corrected downward from 14–0–2: the baseline arm had been handicapped (see round 4), which voids TTU2 and weakens V3.
rounds.gap: Two, both in the winning build. The quote checker FALSE-POSITIVED on V2, flagging a quotation that is verbatim in the reference_lookup output it names — a verifier that cries wolf teaches the reader to ignore it, which costs more than the numbering gains. And on TTU2 the app stamps a green ✓ and “it runs without error” over a reply whose stated sum (854,405) contradicts its own executed output (824,693): the check verifies that no exception was raised, not that the numbers match, so the reassurance fires hardest exactly where the answer is wrong.
rounds.fix: Quoted spans checked character-for-character against captured tool output · citation attributions checked against the passage the marker resolves to · a “Tools used” section that names none of the executed calls is contradicted · assistant markdown wraps and code blocks gain a wrap toggle · the raw-neutral guard widened to the whole renderer · a silent stream counts itself out loud and names its deadline · plans disclose what each step may DO before approval · a terminal outcome is the heaviest text in the block · never-run steps stop presenting their contents as findings

rounds.label: Four reassurances the app had not earned

pair.A: the original baseline, this time WITH the Python runtime it had been missing

rounds.what: Five builders on the two faults blind critics found in round 3’s winner, the tie where a check still could not succeed, a cold boot attributed nowhere, and a plan forecast nothing verified — plus the harness guard that let a handicapped arm score for three rounds.
rounds.findings: The quote checker’s false positive is gone and its true positive survives: on TH1 it now names both an undisclosed tool and an invented quotation, and a critic confirmed neither warning is spurious. The claim check stops at the first unreachable source — 7 searches down to 2, post-answer lockout 21.3 s down to 1.4 s, a 15× difference against the same dead provider. The cold sandbox boot is named and quantified — “started the sandbox in 1.6 s, then failed after 7 ms” — where the baseline still reports a cold call as 8 ms against a warm 20 ms.
rounds.verdict: Round-4 build 13 · baseline 3 · 1 tie, over 17 tasks judged blind against a corrected baseline. More losses than round 3 reported — because round 3 was judged against a handicapped arm and this was not.
rounds.gap: Three losses, and the honest reading differs per task. V3: our run hit the 300 s capture budget mid-verification and a critic judged an unfinished turn; re-captured it finishes at 268 s against the baseline’s 213 s, so we are slower and the tail is still unexplained, but the “never finished” reasoning was partly a capture artifact. V1: our build stated 165°F / 74°C, which appear in none of the retrieved passages, and printed “✎ Revised: 1 unsupported item were sent back for verification or removal” — a claim of resolution that did not occur. That is the same false-assurance species this round set out to kill, in a new place. TH2: the baseline won on a provenance line ours did not print.
rounds.fix: Bracketed citation markers trimmed before a quoted span is checked · printed figures compared against the figures the reply states · the unreachable-source rule inverted so an unlisted error code cannot defeat it · the sandbox boot measured, named and reported beside the run time · a plan step reconciled against the tools it actually ran · validity extended twice: a precondition that did not hold, and a turn that never ended

rounds.label: The verification tail, and a revision that did not happen
rounds.what: V1’s “Revised: 1 unsupported item” on a turn where nothing was revised, and a verification tail long enough to blow a 300-second capture budget on one task and cost 136–190 s on another.
